title: Open (Hasson) laparoscopic port insertion on a model

guidelineVersions: International Society for Gynecologic Endoscopy (ISGE) safe laparoscopic entry guideline summary (2021); accessed 12 October 2026

brief.scenario: You are the core surgical trainee assisting in an elective laparoscopic operation. An examiner plays the supervising surgeon. The simulated patient has a healed lower midline laparotomy scar; site selection has been agreed following senior review.
brief.task: The consultant asks you to demonstrate open (Hasson) umbilical port insertion on an abdominal wall training model, talking through the safety checks, tissue layers, controlled entry, port fixation and initial pneumoperitoneum. Demonstrate only on the model. 9 minutes, plus 1 minute reading.

beforeYouWalkIn.frame: This station assesses controlled, direct-vision peritoneal access, anatomical orientation, safe trocar/cannula placement and recognition that open entry is not injury-proof.
beforeYouWalkIn.trap: Treating the word “open” as a guarantee of avoiding visceral/vascular injury or insufflating without confirming appropriate placement.
beforeYouWalkIn.firstMove: “I will confirm the planned entry site with the supervising surgeon, check previous scars and perform controlled layer-by-layer access under vision.”

flow: Safety brief: review previous operations, operative plan and site; check equipment, positioning and consent.
Prepare field and create controlled umbilical skin incision; dissect through subcutaneous tissue to fascia.
Secure fascia, open fascia and peritoneum carefully under direct vision and confirm a safe opening.
Place and fix Hasson cannula, connect CO₂; verify correct insufflation and operative visibility.
Inspect for entry injury, identify safe pressures appropriate to patient and communicate port-site closure plan.

grid.label: Planning and scar assessment
grid.borderline: Mentions scars without an access plan
grid.pass: Reviews prior surgery and confirms senior-agreed entry site
grid.high: Anticipates adhesions and alternative access with senior input

grid.label: Preparation and asepsis
grid.pass: Checks instruments, consent, positioning, prep and sterile field
grid.high: Uses brief and verbalises contingency if access is unsafe

grid.label: Layer identification
grid.pass: Incises skin and exposes fascia under direct vision
grid.high: Maintains orientation and protects underlying tissue

grid.label: Fascial and peritoneal entry
grid.borderline: Controls fascia but opens peritoneum uncertainly
grid.pass: Secures fascia and opens peritoneum carefully under direct vision
grid.high: Limits instrument depth and actively checks for adherent bowel

grid.label: Cannula placement
grid.pass: Introduces Hasson cannula in controlled manner and fixes securely
grid.high: Maintains seal and anticipates gas leakage or cannula displacement

grid.label: CO₂ and pressure
grid.fail: Insufflates blindly or at inappropriate uncontrolled pressure
grid.pass: Connects CO₂, observes pressure/flow and uses the lowest suitable working pressure with anaesthetic communication
grid.high: Actively adapts pressure to exposure and physiology rather than a rigid universal value

grid.label: Inspection and injury detection
grid.pass: Inspects entry site promptly, stops if injury suspected and alerts senior surgeon
grid.high: Plans immediate structured assessment of bowel/vascular injury with team

grid.label: Technique and risk explanation
grid.pass: Explains open-entry benefits and residual injury risks
grid.high: Compares entry methods without unsupported superiority claims

grid.label: Closure and handover
grid.pass: Plans appropriate fascial closure for port size/site and documents issues
grid.high: Explains port-site hernia risk and confirms closure accountability

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: Show me how you would perform open Hasson entry on this model.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: I do not need to ask about old scars because open entry always avoids adhesions.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: You can see a healed lower midline scar.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: I will not check the instruments or the consent form, or prep and drape; it is only a small cut.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: I will push the instrument through the middle until I reach the cavity.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: I will take a deep cut without holding the tissue up.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: There is a loop of bowel directly beneath the peritoneum.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: That is fine. I will keep going with the port.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: I will push the trocar hard and deep into the abdomen so it cannot slip out.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: Assume a cannula is in place. The pressure rises quickly and the gas flow is poor.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: I will increase the pressure until the abdomen expands.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: Would you inspect the entry site?

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: No. Open insertion cannot cause an internal injury.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: What are the risks of the open technique?

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: There are none. Open entry removes any risk of bowel or vessel injury.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: A skin stitch is enough regardless of fascial defect.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: Show me how you would perform open Hasson entry on this model.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I am the core surgical trainee. I will confirm the consent, prior abdominal surgery and senior-agreed entry site before starting. Was there a previous laparotomy?

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: There is a healed lower midline scar. The site has been agreed after consultant review.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I check the camera system, Hasson cannula, sutures, graspers, CO₂ connections and sterile preparation. I confirm the patient is positioned and the team is ready.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I make a controlled skin incision, dissect through the subcutaneous tissue and identify the fascia. I avoid plunging instruments toward the cavity.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: The fascia is exposed. Show the next step.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I grasp and secure the fascia with stay sutures, incise it cautiously and expose then open the peritoneum under direct vision.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: You see bowel immediately beneath the opening.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I stop. I will not push through it. I protect the bowel, reassess the opening and ask the supervising surgeon to assess whether this site is safe before continuing.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: The surgeon helps clear the opening safely.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I insert the blunt Hasson cannula in a controlled manner and secure it with the fascial sutures for a seal.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I connect CO₂ and check pressure, flow and abdominal response rather than assuming the cannula position is correct.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: Flow is poor and the pressure rises rapidly.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I stop insufflation and check cannula position, tubing, obstruction and gas flow; I tell the consultant. I do not force insufflation.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: After correction, insufflation is smooth and entry can be inspected.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I inspect the entry region laparoscopically for injury and continue only if there is no concern. If I suspected bowel or vascular injury I would stop and escalate immediately.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Open access offers direct exposure but does not remove injury risk, particularly where adhesions are possible.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: At the end we will close the fascial defect appropriately, check haemostasis and document entry difficulty or complications.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: Show me how you would perform open Hasson entry on this model.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Before touching the model, I want a deliberate access plan: prior incisions, possible adhesions, hernias and whether the proposed umbilical site remains suitable, or whether a left upper quadrant (Palmer's point) entry would be safer. Was the lower abdominal scar assessed?

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: There is a healed lower midline scar. The consultant agreed the entry site.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: I confirm the team brief, consent, prophylaxis if prescribed for the operation, patient positioning, functioning laparoscope and insufflator, the Hasson cannula, stay sutures and a clear plan for failed entry. The field is prepared and sterile.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: I make a modest skin incision and dissect the tissue layer by layer with controlled traction until the fascial plane is visible. I identify tissue rather than relying on a memorised depth.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: I secure the fascial edges with stay sutures, open fascia incrementally and lift the peritoneum before deliberately entering under direct vision, always considering adherent viscera.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: You see bowel immediately beneath the opening.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: That changes the plan. I stop at this point and protect the bowel. I will not stretch or insert a port against it. I ask the consultant to inspect and consider another entry strategy if safe exposure cannot be obtained.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: The consultant confirms a safe space can be developed.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: I advance the blunt cannula only into the confirmed opening, seat it stably, anchor it with the stay sutures and check the seal without uncontrolled force.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: I request gentle CO₂ insufflation and watch pressure and flow with the anaesthetist; we aim for the lowest pressure that permits safe visualisation and patient tolerance.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: Flow is poor and pressure rises rapidly.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Stop CO₂ now. Rapid pressure rise is not a cue to increase the target. Check for tubing obstruction, a blocked or malpositioned cannula and extraperitoneal insufflation; reassess under direct vision and discuss with the consultant.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: The issue is corrected and laparoscopic view is satisfactory.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Before further ports, I inspect the entry path and adjacent bowel and vessels for damage. If any concern exists, I stop, communicate it and assess the injury openly and systematically.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Neither open nor closed techniques abolish visceral or vascular injury risk; selection depends on anatomy, operative history and operator expertise.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Finally I ensure the port is secure, plan deliberate fascial closure of an appropriate defect, and document site, technique, access difficulty and any concern for complications.

failures.move: Forcing access despite visible bowel directly under the peritoneum.
Increasing insufflation pressure despite rapid rise and poor flow without checking placement.
Ignoring suspicion of bowel or vascular injury.
failures.consequence: Delays recognition of potentially life-threatening complication.

recovery.when: If you cannot safely identify a clear plane
recovery.line: I cannot safely identify a clear plane: I will stop, protect the tissue and get the consultant to reassess the entry site.

recovery.when: If the pressure/flow behaviour is abnormal
recovery.line: The pressure/flow behaviour is abnormal: stop CO₂ and check cannula placement before any further insufflation.

knowledge.fact: Open Hasson entry is a mini-laparotomy with direct placement of a cannula and subsequent pneumoperitoneum.
Suspected or known adhesions contraindicate umbilical entry and call for an alternative site; the left upper quadrant (Palmer's point) is the recommended alternative.
Open entry shows no significant difference in visceral or vascular injury rates compared with other methods, and no entry technique can be recommended as the gold standard.
Controlled incision, direct visualisation and avoiding forced instrument advancement are foundational safety principles.
Poor insufflation or difficult cannula placement requires stopping and checking position before escalation of pressure.

recall.think: The first port is the dangerous moment; previous scars may mean adherent bowel.
recall.say: “I will enter in layers under vision and stop if the safe plane disappears.”
do: Secure fascia, open peritoneum cautiously, insert and fix cannula, then check CO₂.

numbers.meaning: ISGE (gynaecological guidance) suggests a transient entry pressure in healthy women
reduced to once all trocars are placed
In this station, use the lowest working pressure that gives a safe view, agreed with the anaesthetist.

recall.trap: An open port is not immunity from bowel or vascular injury.
recall.finish: Inspect the entry site, document any difficulty and ensure appropriate fascial closure.
